rule: A candidate becomes a type when it is seen at 3 or more universities and no existing type captures it (D33). Rechecked after every batch and in the theme review (D34).

candidates.name: Consent before AI recording or transcription
candidates.definition: Instructors or students need permission before using AI to record or transcribe class sessions or meetings.

candidates.name: Ban on a named AI tool
candidates.definition: A specific AI product is banned on university devices or networks.

candidates.name: Instructor must not discuss a referred case with the student
candidates.definition: After referring suspected misuse, instructors do not question or discuss it with the student (the opposite of P57).

candidates.name: Peer duty to report others' misconduct
candidates.definition: Students must report honor-code breaches they observe; may fold into P71.

candidates.name: AI use justified by learning objectives
candidates.definition: AI use must be justified by its relevance to the course learning objectives.

candidates.name: Ban on humanizer tools that evade detection
candidates.definition: Students may not use tools that disguise AI text to evade detectors.

candidates.name: Students run detection on their own work
candidates.definition: Students check their own work with detection or originality tools before submitting.

candidates.name: Label AI-intensive courses
candidates.definition: Courses that use AI heavily are labeled in registration.

candidates.name: Sign an AI-policy agreement
candidates.definition: Students sign or acknowledge the AI policy; may fold into P70.

candidates.name: AI outputs as public records
candidates.definition: AI outputs may be public records under open-records law; may fold into P77.

candidates.name: List all human collaborators
candidates.definition: Collaborative work names every human team member.

candidates.name: Allow AI for routine work already mastered
candidates.definition: AI may do routine calculations or ancillary tasks the student already knows how to do.

candidates.name: Ban AI for studying, allow it for polishing
candidates.definition: The inverse of P12/P14: no AI for learning concepts, but allowed for editing.

candidates.name: Cross-institution coalitions and benchmarking
candidates.definition: Join or benchmark against peer institutions on AI policy.

candidates.name: Student runs similarity or detection checks on own work
candidates.definition: Students or researchers check their own work with similarity or detection tools before submitting.

candidates.name: Tell students how misuse will be detected
candidates.definition: The syllabus says how AI misuse may be detected, and instructors are open about detector use.

candidates.name: Citation does not make AI-written work acceptable
candidates.definition: Attributing AI output does not make submitting it acceptable in certain assignments.

candidates.name: Acknowledge non-use of AI
candidates.definition: Students state that no AI was used.

candidates.name: Report and correct AI errors after submission
candidates.definition: A student who later finds AI errors in submitted work tells the instructor and corrects them.

candidates.name: Group members agree on AI use
candidates.definition: Team members agree among themselves how AI will be used and disclosed, and instructors explain how to handle a teammate's AI use.

candidates.name: Support students' AI-related wellbeing
candidates.definition: Staff recognize AI-related academic, social and emotional challenges and refer students to support.

candidates.name: Apply AI rules consistently across students
candidates.definition: Ad hoc permissions and enforcement apply equally to all students in a course.

candidates.name: Disclosure tiers for research
candidates.definition: Research uses are sorted into must, may and need-not disclose.

candidates.name: Students may not share AI accounts
candidates.definition: Students may not share a chat-model account with another student.

candidates.name: Require multi-factor authentication and security controls for AI
candidates.definition: Technical security controls on AI tools (MFA, firewall, DLP, API registration).

candidates.name: Instructor workload of AI rules
candidates.definition: AI policies, bans or required declarations add grading and checking workload, which instructors should weigh.

candidates.name: Students must be able to justify their AI use
candidates.definition: Students must be ready to explain why their AI use was appropriate.

candidates.name: Weigh mitigating circumstances in sanctions
candidates.definition: Sanctions consider mitigating and aggravating circumstances.

candidates.name: Keep integrity cases confidential
candidates.definition: Information about integrity cases stays confidential.

candidates.name: Notice or consent before using AI detectors
candidates.definition: Students are told in advance, or consent, before their work goes to a detector.

candidates.name: Ban AI for data analysis
candidates.definition: AI may not analyze data, simulation results or draw conclusions (the opposite of P89).

candidates.name: Allow AI for translation
candidates.definition: AI may translate text, with citation or permission.

candidates.name: Signs of AI-written work
candidates.definition: Instructors watch for signs such as missing voice or inconsistent work.

candidates.name: Disseminate AI guidance through a communication plan
candidates.definition: Institution communicates AI guidance through channels, portals or a central page.

candidates.name: Ban AI-generated references
candidates.definition: Students may not use AI to produce references or citations.

candidates.name: State-law limits on AI for political activity
candidates.definition: Employees may not use AI to lobby or express political opinions (state law).

candidates.name: Label synthetic media with provenance
candidates.definition: AI-generated media carries labels or provenance metadata.

candidates.name: Attempted misuse counts as misuse
candidates.definition: Attempting prohibited AI use is treated like completing it.

candidates.name: Prompts must be the student's own work
candidates.definition: Prompts given to AI must be the student's unaided work.

candidates.name: Opting out of AI does not affect grades
candidates.definition: Students who use or do not use AI within policy are graded the same.

candidates.name: Instructors test assignments against AI
candidates.definition: Instructors run their assignments through AI to see what it produces.

candidates.name: Acknowledge diverse views on AI
candidates.definition: The document records that community members hold opposed views on AI.

candidates.name: AI deployment must uphold DEI commitments
candidates.definition: AI use must be consistent with diversity, equity and inclusion commitments.

candidates.name: Register personal-data AI processes
candidates.definition: AI processes using personal data are registered in a data inventory.

candidates.name: Student's own voice as a value
candidates.definition: Students should keep their own voice rather than AI's.
